study type: Secondary analysis of single-centred registry-based surveillance data
exposure: maternal characteristics (e.g., antenatal care status, hypertension, infections)
cohort: The study included all deliveries of intrauterine fetal death at or beyond 22 weeks' gestation and/or birth weight of 500 g or more, conducted at a tertiary care hospital in Nepal between 16 July 2017 and 15 July 2019.
finding: The stillbirth rate was 15 per 1000 births, with maternal hypertension (29.1%) and intrauterine infection (8.9%) being common identified causes, and nearly a third of cases having an unknown cause (31.6%).
mod_finding: The majority of stillbirths (94.9%) occurred via vaginal delivery, with only 5.1% via caesarean section (p<0.0001).
gest_age: 22 weeks' period of gestation or more
